notes: Official plan sheets (Peugeot 'PLAN D'ENTRETIEN', FR, 208 P21E, PureTech 75 BVM5 / 100 BVM6 / 100 EAT8 / 130 EAT8, hosted by forum-peugeot.com, uploaded 2020-05) give identical intervals across 75/100/130 hp. The only difference is a rear-drum removal row on the 75 hp. These are four sheets from one publisher, so they are not independent corroboration of each other. Timing-belt revision timeline, as documented by press and aftermarket sources: (1) original 10 years/175,000 km; (2) from the late-2020 recall, 6 years/100,000 km; (3) Feb 2021 (recall note v5): the belt is checked at every service and stays at 175,000 km/10 years if not replaced; (4) Dec 2022 (recall note 4006/V2): back to 6 years/100,000 km; L'argus (24/03/2024) splits this by production date: up to March 2017 = 10 years/175,000 km, from April 2017 = 6 years/100,000 km. A MY2021 208 II falls in the April-2017+ group. (5) A new belt part reference has been fitted since 20 June 2022, and no source found gives a different interval for it. (6) Warranty (not maintenance): Europe extended to 10 years/175,000 km from 19 March 2024 for engines built April 2014 to 20 June 2022; Israel extended to 10 years/180,000 km (Walla, 14.1.2026). Israel: Lubinski-sourced press (auto.co.il, 20.10.2020) gives 15,000 km or 1 year for the petrol 208, which equals the FR severe plan. No Lubinski-published service booklet for the 208 II was found online. Oil spec per the plan: 0W20 B71 2010 (C5) or 0W30 B71 2312. The 2023+ third-generation EB2 (mild hybrid) uses a timing chain and is not applicable to a MY2021 car.
